verdict.rationale: Svelte ships first-party state management inside the framework itself rather than as a separate package. The $state, $derived and $effect runes provide reactive state, and .svelte.js/.svelte.ts modules let you share reactive state across the app. A community user also reports that Svelte Stores and the Context system work well for sharing state. Missing for 10: first-party docs on the stores API in the evidence, any dedicated standalone state library or app-wide state tooling such as devtools, and independent corroboration of the rune-based app-wide state pattern.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official first-party state management library maintained alongside the framework

citations.quote: The `$state` rune allows you to create _reactive state_, which means that your UI _reacts_ when it changes.
This is useful for creating reusable reactive logic, or sharing reactive state across your app
$derived computes reactive values based on dependencies.
Svelte Stores and the Context system are great for sharing state
